headline: Maui County Liquor Control Commission

meeting.summary: The Liquor Control Commission approved two restaurant liquor licenses, including Star Noodle's post-wildfire move, and deferred the director's evaluation to January.
meeting.recap: The Liquor Control Commission meeting began at 9:02 on Wednesday, December 11, 2024.[[0:00:30]] Star Noodle, impacted by the August 2023 wildfires, asked to move its restaurant liquor license to 1287 Front Street.[[0:05:02]] Staff reported 88 owners and lessees within 500 feet and no protests.[[0:07:00]] The commission voted unanimously to approve the Star Noodle application.[[0:08:01]] The director said agencies outside the department handle those approvals.[[0:09:14]] The commission unanimously approved a liquor license for a ramen restaurant, with a one-year extension.[[0:15:52]] The director reported two vacancies in the licensing section after a staff member resigned.[[0:17:51]] The director said fee payments are due 30 days after a licensee signs for the assessment, and late payments get a 5% increase.[[0:19:58]] The commission voted to accept the director's self-evaluation.[[0:21:59]] Commissioners moved to put the final director evaluation on the January agenda.[[0:24:25]] The motion to defer passed unanimously.[[0:26:58]] The commission voted unanimously to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion) to consider privacy matters and consult its attorney.[[0:28:10]] The commission voted unanimously to close out one of the files discussed in executive session.[[0:29:56]] The meeting adjourned at 11:06.[[0:31:00]]
decided: The commission approved the day's agenda by unanimous roll call vote.
The commission approved the November 13, 2024 minutes by unanimous roll call vote.
The commission confirmed general licensing matters items A through C1 by unanimous roll call vote.
The commission approved the ramen restaurant's liquor license application with a one-year extension by unanimous roll call vote.
The commission accepted the director's self-evaluation.
The motion to defer the final director evaluation to January passed unanimously.
The commission voted unanimously to go into executive session on two files.
The commission voted unanimously to close out a file from its agenda.
meeting.next: The final director evaluation will go on the January agenda. Commissioners can still add written input through the online survey. Staff will provide an updated consolidated review with everyone's comments. The department will present its proposed budget for next fiscal year at next month's meeting.
